beats.text: Marie Curie's notebooks are still radioactive.
beats.note: That part is true. They sit in lead-lined boxes at France's national library in Paris.

beats.text: Visitors sign a liability waiver first.
beats.note: They also wear protective gear to open the boxes.

beats.context: The half-life of radium-226, the most common radium isotope. Her papers are still radioactive after more than a century.

beats.text: She carried radium and polonium in her coat pocket.
beats.note: She also kept them in a desk drawer. The source does not say how the contamination reached each page, so this reel does not guess.

beats.text: Her clothes, furniture and cookbooks are listed as well.
beats.note: ScienceAlert reports that her laboratory notes are still radioactive too.

beats.text: Her research is still giving off its own evidence.
